title: Is the alpha rhythm synchronized across the scalp? EEG coherence, bit-for-bit against scipy

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S002, run R02 (eyes-closed), eight parieto-occipital channels (PO7, PO3, POz, PO4, PO8, O1, Oz, O2), first 10 s at 160 Hz
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: Where the Welch case gave the alpha POWER and the spectrogram its time course, coherence gives its spatial STRUCTURE: how consistently two channels share a phase-and-amplitude relationship at each frequency. On the eight parieto-occipital channels of real eyes-closed EEG, eegCoherence's magnitude-squared coherence reproduces scipy.signal.coherence BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~2e-16 across all 28 pairs) once conventions are matched (symmetric Hann, matched window/overlap, detrend=False; the coherence ratio cancels the window normalization). And the finding: posterior alpha coherence is high (mean 0.63, peaking 0.90 between adjacent occipital channels PO3-O1) -- the eyes-closed alpha rhythm is spatially synchronized across the posterior scalp.

claims.statement: max |eegCoherence - scipy.signal.coherence| over all 28 channel pairs (bit-exact)
mean posterior alpha-band coherence across the 28 pairs -- the eyes-closed alpha synchrony
peak alpha coherence -- the most synchronized pair (adjacent occipital channels PO3-O1)
minimum alpha coherence -- the least synchronized posterior pair
channel pairs in the coherence matrix (8 choose 2)

validation.reference: eegCoherence (magnitude-squared coherence, Welch-averaged cross/auto spectra) is validated against scipy.signal.coherence, the gold-standard implementation. scipy re-computes the pairwise coherence matrix with matched conventions -- symmetric Hann window, matched window length (round(window_sec*sr), forced even) + hop, no detrend (detrend=False) -- band-averaged over the identical 8-13 Hz band. The agreement is BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~2e-16 across all 28 pairs), machine epsilon, because the coherence ratio |Sxy|^2/(Sxx*Syy) cancels the window normalization. The finding: posterior alpha coherence is high (mean 0.63, peaking 0.90 between adjacent occipital channels), the eyes-closed alpha rhythm's spatial synchrony.
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb (PhysioNet), subject S002 run R02 (eyes-closed), eight parieto-occipital channels, 10 s at 160 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) eegCoherence reproduces scipy.signal.coherence bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~2e-16) across all 28 posterior channel pairs; (2) posterior alpha coherence is high (mean 0.63, peak 0.90). HONEST scope: (1) this is the FIRST external-reference (scipy) certification of eegCoherence -- it was internally validated only ('golden'), never against the gold-standard scipy.signal.coherence; the op is NOT new; (2) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- once the conventions are matched (symmetric Hann, matched window/overlap, detrend=False), the op and scipy compute the IDENTICAL magnitude-squared coherence, so the ~2e-16 residual is machine epsilon, not a convention agreement; the match is exact because the coherence RATIO cancels the window normalization; (3) IMPORTANT caveat: magnitude-squared coherence is INFLATED by volume conduction -- a shared source projects to nearby electrodes at zero lag, so high coherence between adjacent channels is not proof of true cortico-cortical coupling; the op also offers imaginary coherence (method='imaginary'), which suppresses the zero-lag volume-conduction component (not used here); (4) the finding -- high posterior alpha coherence -- is the expected eyes-closed spatial synchrony, cross-consistent with the Welch/spectrogram/Hjorth cases on the SAME data; a descriptive spatial pattern on one subject/segment/8 channels, not a clinical claim; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: Magnitude-squared coherence cannot separate genuine coupling from volume conduction (a single source seen by two electrodes). The op's imaginary coherence (method='imaginary') keeps only the lagged (non-zero-phase) component, which volume conduction cannot produce; computing it across the montage -- and contrasting eyes-closed with eyes-open -- would isolate the true posterior alpha network from the shared-source inflation. Documented, not escalated.
